newsitem.title: USA: US high-yld issue demand strong, Comcast trades up.
newsitem.headline: US high-yld issue demand strong, Comcast trades up.

text.p: Brisk demand for U.S. high-yield issues on Monday should be a harbinger for more of the same the rest of this week, with even more aggressive pricings sure to come, dealers said.

Monday's issue of Comcast Cellular Holdings Inc's $1.0 billion 10-year 9-1/2 percent senior note deal reflected the positive buying environment, trading up in early Tuesday trade. The deal, which was well-oversubscribed, was also increased in size by $100 million.
Trade in the Comcast notes was extremely active, traders said, recently quoted at par bid, 101-1/2 offer.

"New issues are still trading very strong," one junk bond trader said. "Accounts are flush with cash, still being somewhat selective, but so far we've seen only moderate supply and things have been firm."

High-yield issues slated to price on Tuesday include Colorado Prime Corp's $100 million 10-year 144A senior notes via a J.P. Morgan Securities group. The issue will be priced around 12 percent with warrants, a source said.
Also, GST Telecom Inc's $230 million 10-year 144A senior secured three-year prefunded notes may be issued as early as Tuesday via Morgan Stanley & Co.

High-grade issuance has been slow to build despite talk of "adequate" investor demand. But two large issues, $800 million in five- and 10-year debt from Dominion Resources Inc unit DR Investment and $300 million 10-year debt from Mellon Bank Corp, are expected to price on Tuesday, according to sources close to the deals.

Mellon's deal, with price talk at 67 to 70 basis points off the Treasury curve, was said to be issue bid in early Tuesday dealings. The deal will price through lead manager Credit Suisse First Boston.
Lehman Brothers is managing the DR Investments issue.
Beyond this week, however, dealers and investors are zoned in on the second wave of big railroad debt, Norfolk Southern Corp's $3.0 billion multi-tranche deal.

Multi-notch downgrades of Norfolk Southern debt by both Moody's Investors Servoce and Standard & Poor's were expected, said syndicate sources, who did not not immediately expect any downgrades to hinder the deal.
Moody's cut Norfolk Southern's senior unsecured debt rating to Baa1 from A1. S&P cut the company's senior debt to BBB-plus from AA-minus.
The issue is expected to price through lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc next week.
